title: Dependency Unwinding Reliability: sprint + workshop plan
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures the proposed cross-functional project for reducing implicit service dependencies, aligning on SLO boundaries, and running a lightweight workshop + sprint to validate dependency unwinding patterns. The aim is to de-risk cascading outages, clarify ownership for critical signals, and produce 3 canonical runbooks and one automated SLO check per critical surface by the end of Q1 2026.

Context (why now):
- Recent incidents highlighted brittle call-chains between routing, model-serving, and cache layers (see postmortem: jira/INC-2026-041).
- Some services inherit SLOs indirectly (via downstream partners) which makes error-budget calculations and oncall handoffs fuzzy.
- Platform is adding more model variants and routing policies; unclear dependencies increase blast radius.

Scope (in/out):
- IN: services with >50 p95 latency impact on hosted inference endpoints and any service that appears in top-10 downstream traces for the last 90 days.
- IN: model routing, KV cache, dedicated capacity allocator, and the request-fanout adapter.
- OUT: unrelated user-facing web UI features, long-term refactors that need >3 months.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 3 representative services complete dependency unwinding pilots with documented sequence diagrams and a validated rollback plan.
- Each pilot produces: one runbook (incorporating automated diagnostics), one compact SLO spec checked into repo, one synthetic test that verifies graceful fallback.
- Post-change incident severity and mean time to detect (MTTD) for pilot services reduced by >=30% in 60 days.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Project lead: Ava Chen (eng-sre) — overall coordination, incident model alignment
- Product liaisons: Priya Kapoor (product-hosted-api), Jordan Patel (product-dedicated) — verify product constraints and customer commitments
- Services owners (example): Mateo Ruiz (routing), Sarah Nguyen (model-serving), Liam O'Sullivan (kv-cache) — implement pilots
- Observability: Kenji Matsuo (observability) — metrics, dashboards, synthetic checks
- Solutions & SRE runbooks: Maya Thompson — consolidate runbooks and runbook review

High-level timeline (6 weeks sprint + workshop):
- Week 0 (prep): identify candidate services (small spreadsheet), collect top traces, invite stakeholders. Owners claimed by end of week.
- Week 1: Dependency mapping workshop (2 hours) — cross-team mapping, highlight unclear handoffs, produce dependency surface map.
- Week 2: Sprint kickoff & design — teams draft unwind plan: sequence diagram, fallback strategy, SLO translation (downstream->owner).
- Weeks 3–5: Implementation sprints (3 x 1-week cycles) — pilots execute: add feature flags, implement graceful degradations, add synthetic tests, update dashboards.
- Week 6: Readout + postpilot retro — capture outcomes, create templated artifacts for scaling.

Workshop agenda (Week 1, 2-hour):
- 0:00–0:10: Context + incident highlights (Ava)
- 0:10–0:30: Walk top-3 trace examples (service owners)
- 0:30–1:00: Breakout A: map caller->callee for each trace; identify ownership gaps
- 1:00–1:20: Breakout B: propose immediate mitigations (timeouts, circuit breakers, fallbacks)
- 1:20–1:40: Align on SLO translation: which team owns which symptom?
- 1:40–2:00: Action items + owners + success signals

Artifact templates to deliver per pilot:
- Dependency diagram (svg/png) + short adjacency list (who calls who, optional sequence steps).
- SLO spec (one-paragraph summary + numeric SLI definitions, target, and alert thresholds).
- Runbook skeleton: detection, mitigation, rollback, postmortem checklist.
- Synthetic check (circa 1–5 minute scenario) and a GitHub action to run it nightly.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Keep changes feature-flagged and reversible. No cluster-wide changes without provable rollback.
- Prefer small, observable changes: add circuit breaker with explicit error codes backpressure, implement short-term client-side caching rather than big refactors.
- Use existing tooling: tracing (zipkin/x-ray), logs in structured JSON, Metrics in Prometheus, dashboards in Grafana.

Monitoring and SLO alignment approach:
- Translate compound downstream SLI (e.g., an edge error rate) into per-service SLIs by tracing sampling + attribution heuristics (observability team to supply sampling rule).
- Where attribution ambiguous, default ownership to caller surface and create a follow-on ticket for deeper instrumentation.
- Add an automated nightly job that computes the pilot SLOs and posts a summary in #reliability-pulse.

Communication plan:
- Pre-workshop invite & context doc (sent by Ava, link in linked_artifacts).
- Daily 15-min standups for pilot owners during Weeks 3–5.
- Weekly digest to exec SRE lead and product liaisons with a one-line status and blockers.
- Postpilot public notes + follow-up actions in Confluence.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: scope creep — Mitigation: strict acceptance criteria and a freeze after Week 2 design decisions.
- Risk: cross-team bandwidth — Mitigation: negotiate 2-day focus windows and leverage SRE on-call to help with lift.
- Risk: instrumentation gaps — Mitigation: fall back to synthetic checks and plan deeper instrumentation in a separate ticket.

Open questions (to resolve in Week 1 workshop):
- Do we treat retries inside caller as part of downstream SLO or a caller responsibility?
- What is the maximum allowable customer-visible fallback behavior before a rollback is mandated?
- How will we credit error-budget impact for partial degradations (non-binary outcomes)?

Next steps (immediate):
- By 2026-01-15: finalize candidate list + owners (Ava)
- Schedule workshop for 2026-01-19 and send pre-reads (observability traces, incident snippets)
- Create starter repo and template PR for SLO spec and runbook (GH PR skeleton: infra/slo-templates)
- Triage any immediate high-risk dependencies flagged in the workshop into quick-fix tickets (<= 1 week TTR goal)

Notes to self / shorthand log (working doc style):
- Keep artifacts small and reproducible — aim for one-runbook + one-test pattern per service so we can scale to 10 services in Q2.
- Avoid long-term refactors in pilot; capture refactor ideas for backlog grooming.
- Remember: default to conservative behavior on customer-facing endpoints.

Attachments / references:
- Incident: jira/INC-2026-041 (trace examples attached)
- Existing SLO guidance: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SLO-GUIDE
- Prototype runbook: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/blob/main/slo-template.md

This is a draft. Expect edits after the Week 1 workshop.
